title: Expected CLI errors
responsibility: Provides the error class used for deliberate CLI failures and the functions to throw or recognize it.

inputs.name: fail.message
inputs.description: The text passed unchanged to the Error constructor, so it becomes the message property that callers read from the thrown ExpectedCliError. fail does no trimming, formatting, length or runtime type check, so only the TypeScript string type constrains it: an empty string is accepted, and a Symbol makes the Error constructor throw a TypeError.
examples: Unit function.errors has no contract section.
Could not parse unit.json: unexpected end of JSON input
Refusing to overwrite an existing unit.json.

inputs.name: isExpectedCliError.error
inputs.description: Any value to test, checked with instanceof against ExpectedCliError, so only instances of that class or of its subclasses return true. Values such as null, undefined, primitives, plain Error objects and objects whose name property is ExpectedCliError return false.
inputs.unknownReason: The type guard may receive any caught value and narrows it using an instanceof check.

outputs.name: fail
outputs.description: fail is declared to return never and never returns normally: it always throws a new ExpectedCliError built from the supplied message. No value is produced, so callers cannot use a return value from it.

outputs.name: isExpectedCliError
outputs.description: The boolean result of the instanceof check, declared as a type predicate so that a true result narrows the argument to ExpectedCliError in TypeScript. It is false for every other value, including plain Error objects.

errors.name: ExpectedCliError
errors.description: The Error subclass thrown by fail, with its name property set to ExpectedCliError. It is the only error the implementation throws by design, and fail throws it on every call.
